Practical Chemistry We have, No. of gm equivalent of acid Normality of acid = Volume of solution in litre No. of gm equivalent of acid = Normality of acid x Volume of acid solution in litre Similarly, No. of gm equivalent of base = Normality of base x Volume of base solution in litre At equivalence point, No. of gm equivalent of acid = No. of gm equivalent of base or, Normality of acid = Normality of base x Volume of base in litre x Volume of acid in litre or, Normality of acid = Normality of base x Volume of base in ml x Volume of acid in ml (Where, MI and M2 refer to molarity)

But the equation VIMI = V2M2 does not always hold true at the end point because at the end point, the no. of gm moles of a substance may or may not be equal to that of another substance. This equation, however, can be used in dilution.

Redox Titration The titration in which an oxidising agent and a reducing agent are made to react each other is called redox titration. Here, the redox reaction takes place completely at the end point. For example: titration of KMn04 solution (oxidising agent) vs. oxalic acid solution (reducing agent). 21<Mn04 + 3H2S04 + (COOH)2 2H20 K2S04 + 2MnS04 + IOH20 + 2C02 pink colourless Here, KMn04 acts as self-indicator owing to its pink colour.
Theory of Chemical Indicators An indicator works within a pH range and therefore, helps to predict the end point.

Volumetric Analysis An indicator itself acts as a weak acid or a weak base. For example: methyl orange acts as a weak base and phenolphthalein acts as a weak acid. Methyl orange, in aqueous medium, ionises as below: orange yellow pink [Me+l [OHI- [MeOH1 On adding a base, the hydroxyl ion concentration increases and therefore the equilibrium shifts towards backward direction. Therefore, methyl orange shows light yellow colour in basic medium On adding an acid, the hydrogen ion consumes hydroxyl ion to form water and therefore, the equilibrium shifts towards forward direction.
Hence, methyl orange exhibits pink colour in acidic medium.
Phenolphthalein, in aqueous medium, ionizes as below:

HPh colourless pink On adding an acid, the equilibrium shifts towards left and the solution will be colourless. If a base is added, OH- ion of the base is consumed by .H+ ion of phenolphthalein to form water molecule. This means, the equilibrium shifts towards right and the concentraåon of Ph - ion increases. Therefore, the indicator shows pink colouration in basic medium.

Selection of an Indicator For the selection of an indicator, required for a particular titration, a curve is drawn by taking the volume of alkali along X-axis and pH value along Y-axis. This curve is called as titration curve. As the alkali is added to the acid taken in a conical flask, the pH of the solution increases and different types of curves will be obtained in different acid-base titrations.
The steep rise in pH in the curve corresponds to the end point of titration.
The pH range at the end point is compared with the pH range of each indicator and the selection of a suitable indicator is carried out.
1. Titration of a strong acid and a strong base (HCl Vs. NaOH)

On drawing the titration curve the steep rise in pH is found to be in between 3-11 i.e., the pH range at the end point is 3-11. Therefore, either of the indicators (methyl orange or phenolphthalein) can be used in the titration.
Practical Chemistry Titration of a strong acid and a weak base (HCl Vs. NazC03)
On drawing the titration curve the steep rise in pH is found to be in between 3-8 i.e., the pH range at the end point is 3-8. Thus; methyl orange is used as an indicator in this titration.
Titration of a weak acid and a strong base (Oxalic acid Vs. NaOH)
On drawing the titration curve the steep rise in pH is found to be in between 6-11 i.e., the pH range is 6-11. Thus, phenolphthalein is used in this titration.
Titration of a weak acid and a weak base (Oxalic acid Vs. Na2C03)

On drawing the titration curve the steep rise in pH is found to be in between 6-8 i.e., the pH range is 6-8. Since pH range of no indicator matches this pH range, the titration between a weak acid and a weak base can not be done.
